One-sentence judgment: secondary school career and technical education teachers are not about 'finishing the textbook' — they teach the knowledge and skills of an occupational or technical field to adolescents at the secondary school stage, and are responsible for curriculum objectives, practical training safety, student records, and assessment quality. O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Four (considerable preparation, SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), with no Bright Outlook designation, and an interest code of SCA (social, conventional, artistic). The core boundary is: teacher qualification and the subjects and school level taught must be obtained item by item under local rules, and student assessment and promotion decisions, the handling and reporting of student-protection matters, and the conditions under which practical training equipment may be used are different responsibilities, and teachers cannot exceed their authority to replace the school or competent authority in handling them.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to explain the same thing repeatedly for students at different ability levels and adjust your explanation, and can attend to both learning progress and personal safety in the classroom and at the practical training site (the O*NET work context shows an interest code with social highest at 100, work activity teaching and instructing others at 94, 82% in continuous contact with others, 73% making a public speech every day, and 80% working more than 40 hours per week); you are willing to record student performance and attendance and assessment rationale faithfully and completely, accept working to curriculum standards and school policy, and report per procedure rather than handling it yourself when a student shows an anomaly or is suspected of being harmed.

Conditions for pausing large investments first: you have not yet completed a full closed-loop exercise from curriculum objective setting and lesson planning and practical training safety planning to assessment design and records and communication; or you are unwilling to record and report faithfully per policy, unwilling to repeatedly stress safety procedures during practical training, or unwilling to accept questions from parents and colleagues; also, knowing a craft or having done industry work must not be treated as proof that you already have classroom management and student guidance ability.

Education, qualification, and authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Four (considerable preparation, SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), and the O*NET education survey shows 40% of respondents saying a bachelor's degree is needed, 23% a master's degree, and 13% an associate degree or other two-year credential; this occupation's page lists 1 apprenticeship direction (Agriculture Education Instructor) and 9 certifications (including National Board Certification - Career & Technical Education, Praxis Subject Assessment, Microsoft Certified Educator, Certified in Family and Consumer Sciences, and others). In mainland China, teaching requires obtaining teacher qualification for the corresponding school level and subject under the teacher qualification system and meeting school recruitment and employment conditions; teacher qualification does not equal hiring or the teaching level and subject scope or homeroom or practical training guidance authorization, nor does it equal the school's approval to offer a specific practical training project.

One sentence: this is a position that turns 'whether this career or technical course has really been learned by students, and whether the process is safe and traceable' into reviewable evidence, with outputs being curriculum objectives and lesson plans, classroom and practical training records, student assessment and grade rationale, student performance and attendance records, practical training safety and equipment inspection records, and communication records with students and parents and colleagues; it is not a school management or curriculum approval role, nor does it replace the school's or competent authority's handling and reporting of student-protection matters. For mainland China this page publishes no occupation-level wage figure and only registers the framing and gap with a visible marker.

The work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, classroom teaching (setting curriculum objectives and lesson plans, lecturing and demonstrating and discussing, assigning and grading homework and tests, assessing student progress, and adjusting pace to curriculum standards); second, practical training and safety guidance (preparing and maintaining practical training equipment and materials, demonstrating and supervising equipment use and care, checking site and equipment hazards, and establishing and enforcing classroom and practical training site order and safety procedures); third, records and communication (maintaining student enrollment and performance and attendance and assessment records, communicating with parents or guardians and colleagues and administrators, participating in individualized support and tutoring and job placement referrals, and reporting exceptions per procedure). All three share the same chain centered on curriculum objectives, student learning evidence, and traceable records.
Classroom teaching

Set course and unit objectives → prepare lesson plans and teaching materials → lecture and demonstrate and run group practice → assign and grade homework and tests → adjust pace and provide individual tutoring based on assessment results → document teaching and student progress
Practical training and safety guidance

Editorial practical training process: check equipment and site protection before class, demonstrate, and supervise safe student use; Article 18 of China's school safety measures requires facilities with hidden hazards to be taken out of use and repaired or replaced or protected or marked with warnings in good time, and specific use suspension and restoration follow school policy and this page does not assign teachers repair authority.

Collect evidence of student performance and attendance and assessment → score against standards and state the rationale → maintain enrollment and grade and communication records → communicate progress and improvement points with students and parents or guardians → collaborate with colleagues and counselors and administrators on individual needs → report exceptions per procedure and keep records

Secondary school career and technical education teachers center on curriculum objectives, student learning evidence, and traceable records; training and development specialists address in-service staff job competence improvement, educational guidance and career counselors address students' further-education and career counseling, and business teachers and computer science teachers and family and consumer sciences teachers at the higher education stage address subject teaching, with research duties depending on the actual position, while instructional coordinators handle curriculum and teaching coordination and teacher training. Similar names or adjacency in the education chain do not mean that teacher qualification, teaching scope, assessment authority, and student-protection handling authority are interchangeable.
Core purpose

To let secondary school students truly acquire verifiable knowledge and skills in an occupational or technical field and complete practical training safely: curriculum objectives and lesson plans ensure teaching has a basis, assessment and records make learning visible and reviewable, and safety procedures and order management keep the process controllable.
Main subjects and basis

The subjects are secondary school students and classes and practical training groups, as well as curriculum standards and textbooks and lesson plans, practical training equipment and tools and materials and protective equipment, classrooms and laboratories and workshop sites, test and homework and assessment standards, enrollment and grade and attendance and communication records, and individualized support and tutoring and job placement and extracurricular activity arrangements; the basis is the local teacher qualification and teaching scope rules, school and district policies and administrative regulations, curriculum standards and teaching syllabi, practical training safety and equipment operation and site management rules, student record and privacy and mandatory reporting requirements, and the school's approval system for courses and activities.
Core process

Set curriculum objectives, prepare lesson plans and materials, lecture and demonstrate, organize practical training and circulate for safety, assign and grade homework and tests, assess and record student progress, communicate with parents and colleagues, and report exceptions per procedure and supplement records.
Main outputs

Curriculum objectives and lesson plans and teaching materials, classroom and practical training records, test and homework and assessment results and scoring rationale, student performance and attendance and enrollment records, practical training equipment and site inspection and maintenance records, communication records with students and parents or guardians, individualized support and tutoring and job placement and referral records, and exception and reporting records.
Accountable parties

Teachers are responsible for teaching and assessment and safety supervision according to the school's division of labor; the principal accountability system in Article 16 of the school safety measures cannot erase teachers' own duties. Article 48 of the school protection regulations requires staff to handle promptly, within the scope of their own work, any infringement of student rights they discover, and to report promptly what is beyond or cannot be handled; Article 49 requires aid first. Article 11 of China's Law on the Protection of Minors requires units in close contact with minors and their staff to report immediately to public security and civil affairs and education and other relevant departments upon discovering harm or suspected harm or other danger; internal school reporting cannot replace or delay the statutory report, and urgent danger must be aided promptly without waiting for internal school approval.
Authority and approval

Article 11 of China's Teachers Law distinguishes junior secondary (junior college or above) from general education and specialized courses at senior secondary and secondary vocational schools (bachelor's or above); secondary vocational practicum supervision under Article 7 of the implementing measures requires secondary vocational graduation or above and under Article 7 of the regulations requires assistant engineer or above or intermediate worker level or above, with education relaxation for special skills requiring approval. Article 5 of the qualification regulations provides mutual recognition between senior secondary and secondary vocational teacher qualifications, and practicum supervision qualification application has separate limits; qualification does not equal school hiring or authority over all courses. Unsafe facilities are taken out of use and reported according to law; student danger is aided and reported promptly, without waiting for course approval first.
Conclusion boundaries

Curriculum records and assessment results describe how a student performed under the given curriculum standard, class profile, and teaching conditions; they are not a final characterization of the student's ability, nor do they replace the school's and competent authority's handling of student-protection matters, and they are updated as curriculum standards, class composition, and teaching arrangements change; when citing, state the curriculum standard version, the assessment method, and the record period at the same time.

Before starting, verify at least six items: job duties (leaning toward career and technical course teaching, practical training and equipment safety guidance, student guidance and further-education and employment counseling, curriculum and teaching project design, or teaching work coordination), the required teacher qualification and teaching level and subject scope, practical training site and equipment conditions and the division of safety responsibility, class size and class hours and workload arrangements, student record and communication and mandatory reporting requirements, and whether the role includes homeroom or extracurricular activity or school-enterprise cooperation duties.
Occupational framing

This frozen identity is 25-2032.00 secondary school CTE teacher, which shares the same SOC as 0140 but keeps an independent asset. O*NET Job Zone4, no Bright Outlook designation, education services 99% / other 1%. O*NET interest SCA: S100/C49/A41/I40/R31/E25; the specific interests teaching 99, social service 72, professional counseling 69, and public speaking 60 are separate dimensions and not S sub-items or individual competence thresholds. Chinese secondary vocational and senior secondary related courses can serve as a duty comparison, but no one-to-one occupational wage mapping has been established.
Education and training pathways

The O*NET new-hire education requirement Q&A shows 40% bachelor's, 23% master's, and 13% associate degree, which is not the incumbent educational composition; Job Zone4 is a cross-occupational preparation zone, and the 1 Agriculture Education Instructor apprenticeship example does not prove current enrollment or that everyone must complete it. U.S. BLS summarizes the commonly required bachelor's degree and work experience in the field taught; public school state qualification and licensure conditions vary by state, and teaching internships and background checks and examinations must be verified for the specific route, while the 9 related certifications and examinations are not uniformly state licenses or mandatory for everyone in this occupation. Article 5 of the qualification regulations provides mutual recognition between senior secondary and secondary vocational teacher qualifications, and separate restrictions apply to the use of practicum-supervision qualifications; qualification does not equal school hiring or authority over all courses. Article 46 of China's Vocational Education Law separately requires specialized course teachers (including practicum supervision) to have corresponding practical experience and technical skills, and qualified industry personnel who have undergone educational and teaching ability training may serve full-time or part-time, and education requirements for obtaining qualifications to teach specialized subjects may be lowered as appropriate; industry experience does not automatically obtain qualification.
Methods and tools

The O*NET technology list names 12 categories of software skills, and the Hot Technologies page lists 7 items (Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D, Google Docs, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Office software, Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft PowerPoint, and Microsoft Word), and that page gives no shares (the data source is 2025 U.S. job postings from Lightcast). On-site methods and tools center on practical training equipment and tools and protective equipment, classroom lecturing and demonstration equipment, learning management and grade and attendance record systems, test and homework and assessment tools, curriculum standards and textbooks and lesson plan materials, and channels for communicating with parents. A hiring-demand tag indicates frequency of appearance in employer job postings and does not mean the institution has deployed that type of tool or that the position has been displaced.
Safety and work permits

Work is mainly fixed in-school schedules and being on site, while also carrying after-class workload such as lesson preparation and grading and communication; the main load comes from long periods of standing and talking, continuous interpersonal interaction and emotional labor, and watching several students' safety at the same time at the practical training site. O*NET work context shows: 82% in continuous contact with others; 80% working more than 40 hours per week; 73% making a public speech every day; 67% having face-to-face discussions every day; 59% making decisions every day that affect others or organizational resources or reputation; 55% indoors in a controlled environment every day; 51% dealing with unpleasant or angry or discourteous people at least once a week but not every day; 51% considering coordinating or leading others extremely important; 48% keeping a moderate close distance (within arm's reach) with others; 43% reporting a lot of freedom over tasks and priorities; 39% having extremely high responsibility for the health and safety of other workers; 38% reporting a lot of decision freedom; 38% standing about half the time; 33% exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise every day. Work requirements follow curriculum standards and school policy, and practical training must implement protection and supervision per equipment and site safety procedures; when a student safety anomaly is found, protect the student first and then report. Pay and hours

U.S. secondary school CTE usually follows the school schedule, but lesson preparation and home-school communication happen before and after class; O*NET shows NET80% working more than 40 hours per week, and the traditional academic-year holiday is not a legally uniform arrangement for all schools. The U.S. 2025 median annual wage is 66,270 USD, annual wage percentiles only. The NBS 2025 education sector urban non-private unit average annual wage is 133,539 yuan and the private unit figure is 63,908 yuan, both pretax annual averages and multi-occupation sector references; they are not this occupation's average or median or starting or monthly wage. Secondary school career and technical education teachers (O*NET-SOC 25-2032.00, Career/Technical Education Teachers, Secondary School) teach occupational and vocational skills and career or technical subjects to students at the secondary school stage. Daily work includes: providing individual and group instruction to students using multiple teaching methods such as lecture and discussion and demonstration; establishing and enforcing behavioral rules and procedures that maintain student order; preparing materials and the classroom for classroom activities; observing and evaluating students' performance and behavior and social development and physical health; teaching the knowledge and skills required for a specific occupation or occupational field through systematic instruction, discussion, audiovisual presentations, and laboratory and workshop and on-site learning plans; instructing and monitoring students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injuries and damage; setting clear objectives for all lessons and units and projects and communicating them to students; using computers and audiovisual aids and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations; instructing and counseling students with adjustment or academic problems or special academic interests; maintaining accurate and complete student records as required by law and district policy and administrative regulations; planning and conducting a balanced program of instruction and demonstration and work time that provides students with opportunities to observe and question and investigate; preparing and administering and grading tests and assignments to evaluate students' progress; assigning and grading class work and homework; enforcing all administrative policies and rules governing students; providing assistive devices and supportive technology and assistance accessing facilities to students with disabilities; preparing students for promotion to higher grades by encouraging them to explore learning opportunities and to persevere with challenging tasks; planning and supervising class projects and field trips and guest lectures and other experiential activities and guiding students in learning from them; conferring with parents or guardians and other teachers and counselors and administrators to resolve students' behavioral and academic problems; keeping up with education trends and developments in the professional field taught; planning and supervising work experience programs in businesses and industrial workshops and school laboratories; meeting with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress; preparing and implementing remedial programs for students requiring extra help; establishing course objectives and outlines following curriculum guidelines or requirements of the state and school; meeting with parents or guardians to discuss their children's progress and to determine priorities and resource needs; arranging job placements for students or referring them to employment placement services; selecting and ordering and storing and issuing and inventorying classroom equipment and materials and supplies; advising student clubs and student organizations and academic competitions and other extracurricular activities; collaborating with other teachers and administrators in the development and evaluation and revision of secondary school programs; attending professional meetings and educational conferences and teacher training workshops to maintain and improve professional competence; meeting with other staff members to plan and schedule lessons following approved curricula; preparing reports on students and activities as required by administration; and attending staff meetings and serving on committees as required, and carrying administrative duties such as library assistance and hallway and cafeteria monitoring and bus loading and unloading. It carries responsibility for student protection and teaching quality and teaching scope, but does not replace the school's and competent authority's responsibility for curriculum approval and the handling of student-protection matters and personnel management.

paragraphs: This page compares secondary school career and technical education teachers with six adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference is a better fit for. Adjacent directions are described by their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean that job titles or teacher qualifications are interchangeable.

Evidence note: occupational direction and core outputs are based on O*NET-SOC 25-2032.00 and the official descriptions of adjacent entries (U.S. framing); the adjacent occupations listed by this evidence route are training and development specialists, educational guidance and career counselors, business teachers (higher education), computer science teachers (higher education), and family and consumer sciences teachers (higher education), with instructional coordinators as a related O*NET occupation; teacher qualification and teaching scope, student assessment and promotion decisions, and the handling and reporting authority for student-protection matters must be verified separately under each jurisdiction and school policy, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut for switching careers.

The table below compares the differences in duties and outputs between secondary school career and technical education teachers and adjacent directions; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, what the work is accountable for, and the required qualifications, not how similar the job titles sound.

Training and development specialists design and deliver in-service training inside an organization and are employed by enterprises and institutions; this occupation serves adolescent students at the secondary school stage and is bound by curriculum standards and teacher qualification and school policy.

If you would rather do training and capability improvement for in-service staff, examine the training and development specialist direction first; if you would rather teach career and technical courses in a secondary school classroom, examine this occupation first.
Job competence improvement for in-service staff, with outputs mainly training plans and training effectiveness evaluation.
Training and development specialists

Educational guidance and career counselors work mainly through individual and group counseling, directly addressing students' further-education and career choices; this occupation is centered on course teaching and assessment, with student guidance only part of its duties.

If you would rather do further-education and career counseling and individual tutoring, examine the educational guidance and career counselor direction first; if you would rather carry responsibility for course teaching and assessment, examine this occupation first.
Providing further-education and career counseling and individual tutoring, with outputs mainly counseling records and individualized plans.
Educational guidance and career counselors

Business teachers (higher education) usually require an advanced degree in the discipline and carry research and academic publication requirements, teaching university and graduate students; this occupation teaches secondary school students, with the focus on career and technical skills and practical training safety.

If you would rather do subject teaching and research in a university, examine the business teacher (higher education) direction first (usually requiring a higher degree); if you would rather do career and technical education in a secondary school, examine this occupation first.
Teaching business courses and conducting research at the higher education stage, with outputs mainly course teaching and academic results.

entries.answer: Teaching occupational and vocational skills and career or technical subjects at the secondary school level: providing individual and group instruction to students using methods such as lecture and discussion and demonstration; establishing and enforcing behavioral rules and procedures that maintain order; preparing materials and the classroom for classroom activities; observing and evaluating students' performance and behavior and social development and physical health; teaching the knowledge and skills required for a specific occupational field through systematic plans; instructing and monitoring students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injuries and damage; setting clear objectives for lessons and units and projects and communicating them to students; preparing and administering and grading tests and assignments; assigning and grading class work and homework; providing assistive devices and supportive technology and assistance accessing facilities to students with disabilities; conferring with parents or guardians and other teachers and counselors and administrators to resolve students' behavioral and academic problems; planning and supervising class projects and field trips and work experience programs; maintaining student records per law and district policy; advising student clubs and extracurricular activities; and attending teaching research and training and staff meetings.
entries.question: What does a secondary school career and technical education teacher do every day?

entries.answer: The main risks are student injury from insufficient practical training site supervision, privacy consequences from improper handling of student records and family information, unfair or inaccurate assessment and grade handling, practical training equipment and site hazards not being removed in time, handling student-protection matters beyond one's authority or delaying reports, and skill depreciation as curriculum standards and technology update; control depends on pre-class equipment and site checks, continuous circulation and correction while students work, maintaining and accessing student records per policy, scoring against published standards with the rationale kept, protecting students first and reporting per procedure when a student is suspected of being harmed, and continuous participation in teaching research and training.
entries.question: What risks does this work most need to watch for in advance?

entries.answer: The fit signals are being able to adjust your explanation for students at different ability levels and maintain classroom order, being willing to keep circulating at the practical training site and correct unsafe behavior, and being able to report per procedure rather than handling it yourself when a student shows an anomaly; what matters is whether you have reviewable lesson plans and classroom records and assessment and scoring rationale and student records and actual teaching performance, not just an interest in a craft or industry experience.
entries.question: How do I judge whether this work suits me?

entries.answer: Steps such as first drafts of lesson plans and handouts and exercises, learning material retrieval and organizing, first drafts of tests and grade statistics, notice and communication text drafting, and attendance and homework ledger organizing can be assisted; curriculum objective setting and teaching judgments, confirmation of learning evidence, assessment and promotion recommendations, on-site practical training safety judgments, and student-protection reporting are still verified and borne by a certified teacher per school policy.

entries.answer: Curriculum objectives and teaching judgments, evaluation of student performance and behavior, assessment standards and grade determination and changes, promotion and referral recommendations, on-site practical training safety judgments and decisions to stop use, the records and time limits for student records and reporting, and consistency checks between automated scoring results and original assignments must all be completed by authorized people with a paper trail.

subject.name: Career/technical education teachers, secondary school
subject.summary: This page's entry corresponds to secondary school career and technical education teachers (O*NET-SOC 25-2032.00, Career/Technical Education Teachers, Secondary School): teaching occupational and vocational skills and career or technical subjects to students at the secondary school level — providing individual and group instruction using lecture and discussion and demonstration, setting course and unit objectives and preparing lesson plans and materials, establishing and enforcing behavioral rules that maintain classroom and practical training order, instructing and monitoring students in the use and care of equipment to prevent injuries and damage, observing and evaluating student performance and behavior and social development and physical health, preparing and grading tests and assignments, maintaining student records per law and district policy, and communicating student progress with parents or guardians and colleagues; work is mainly fixed in-school schedules (82% in continuous contact with others, 73% making a public speech every day, 80% working more than 40 hours per week, 39% having extremely high responsibility for the health and safety of others), and its duties do not replace the school's and competent authority's responsibility for curriculum approval and personnel management, with student-protection matters handled by designated positions per policy.
